items.stem: Define the term “chlorophyll a”.
items.answer: The chief pigment of photosynthesis, which appears bright or blue-green in chromatography.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the chief pigment of photosynthesis, which appears bright or blue-green in chromatography.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about early experiments, the site of photosynthesis and pigments is correct?
items.answer: Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis.
items.markingKey: (b) Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis. The other statements are false. Van Niel and later isotope studies showed the O₂ comes from H₂O. The bacteria accumulated mainly in the blue and red regions of the spectrum. It occurs in leaves and also in other green parts of the plant.
options: Photosynthesis occurs only in the leaves of plants.
Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis.
The O₂ released in photosynthesis comes from CO₂.
Engelmann found that aerobic bacteria accumulated mainly in the green region of light.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis.
Reason (R): Engelmann found that aerobic bacteria accumulated mainly in the green region of light.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The bacteria accumulated mainly in the blue and red regions of the spectrum.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The dark reactions of photosynthesis occur in the grana.”
items.answer: The light reactions occur in the grana; enzymatic (dark) reactions occur in the stroma.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The light reactions occur in the grana; enzymatic (dark) reactions occur in the stroma.

items.stem: In a paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, one band is described: absorbs a wider range of wavelengths; accessory pigment. Identify the pigment.
items.answer: xanthophylls
items.markingKey: (a) Xanthophylls: absorbs a wider range of wavelengths; accessory pigment.
options: xanthophylls
carotenoids
chlorophyll b
chlorophyll a

items.stem:
In a paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, one band is described: protects chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation; absorbs a wider range of wavelengths; yellow to yellow-orange colour.
(i) Identify the pigment. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were xanthophylls? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Carotenoids (ii) accessory pigment (iii) protects chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation; yellow colour
items.markingKey: (i) carotenoids – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: accessory pigment – 1 mark. (iii) for xanthophylls: yellow colour; accessory pigment; absorbs a wider range of wavelengths – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which term describes pigments such as chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids that absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a?
items.answer: accessory pigments
items.markingKey: (c) Accessory pigments: pigments such as chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids that absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a.
options: stroma lamellae
grana
accessory pigments
chlorophyll a

items.stem: In a paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, one band is described: yellow to yellow-orange colour; accessory pigment; protects chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation. Identify the pigment. Give a reason.
items.answer: Carotenoids
items.markingKey: 1 mark: carotenoids; 1 mark: the features yellow to yellow-orange colour; accessory pigment; protects chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Leaves appear green.
Reason (R): Chlorophylls absorb mainly blue and red light and reflect green light.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Green light is not absorbed.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Distinguish between an absorption spectrum and an action spectrum. What does their overlap indicate?
items.answer: Absorption spectrum – ability of a pigment to absorb different wavelengths; action spectrum – rate of photosynthesis at different wavelengths. They largely overlap for chlorophyll a, showing chlorophyll a is the chief pigment and most photosynthesis occurs in blue and red light.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Explain the term “photophosphorylation”.
items.answer: The synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the light reaction is correct?
items.answer: The ATP synthase enzyme has a transmembrane channel CF₀ and a CF₁ part protruding into the stroma.
items.markingKey: (c) The ATP synthase enzyme has a transmembrane channel CF₀ and a CF₁ part protruding into the stroma. The other statements are false. Only ATP is synthesised; NADPH is formed in non-cyclic photophosphorylation. Stroma lamellae lack PS II and NADP reductase; they carry out cyclic flow only. They are named in the order of their discovery, not their function.
options: Cyclic photophosphorylation produces both ATP and NADPH.
PS I and PS II are named in the order they act in electron flow.
The ATP synthase enzyme has a transmembrane channel CF₀ and a CF₁ part protruding into the stroma.
The stroma lamellae have both PS I and PS II and NADP reductase.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The water-splitting complex is on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.
Reason (R): Protons accumulate in the stroma during the light reaction.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Protons accumulate in the lumen of the thylakoid; the stroma becomes poorer in H⁺.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Photolysis of water is associated with PS I.”
items.answer: Photolysis of water is associated with PS II.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Photolysis of water is associated with PS II.

items.stem: What three events create the proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane?
items.answer: Splitting of water on the inner side releases H⁺ in the lumen; the electron carrier transfers H⁺ from stroma to lumen as electrons move through the photosystems; NADP reductase on the stroma side removes H⁺ from the stroma while reducing NADP⁺.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Cyclic photophosphorylation does not produce NADPH.
Reason (R): In the cyclic flow electrons from PS I return to PS I via the ETS.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Electrons do not reach NADP⁺.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
A process of the light reaction has these features: only PS I involved; occurs in stroma lamellae; only ATP formed.
(i) Identify the process. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were photolysis of water? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Cyclic photophosphorylation (ii) electrons cycle back to PS I (iii) releases H⁺, [O] and electrons; occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane
items.markingKey: (i) cyclic photophosphorylation – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: electrons cycle back to PS I – 1 mark. (iii) for photolysis of water: associated with PS II; occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane; releases H⁺, [O] and electrons – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between non-cyclic photophosphorylation and photolysis of water on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A process of the light reaction has these features: electrons from water reach NADP⁺. Identify the process – non-cyclic photophosphorylation or photolysis of water? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Non-cyclic photophosphorylation: both PS II and PS I involved; electrons from water reach NADP⁺; forms ATP and NADPH. Photolysis of water: associated with PS II; occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane; releases H⁺, [O] and electrons. (b) Non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: non-cyclic photophosphorylation; 1 mark: “electrons from water reach NADP⁺” is a feature of non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

items.stem: A process of the light reaction has these features: electrons from water reach NADP⁺; both PS II and PS I involved; O₂ is released. Identify the process. Give a reason.
items.answer: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation
items.markingKey: 1 mark: non-cyclic photophosphorylation; 1 mark: the features electrons from water reach NADP⁺; both PS II and PS I involved; O₂ is released are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which term describes groups of pigment molecules bound to proteins in PS I and PS II that make up antennae?
items.answer: light-harvesting complexes (LHC)
items.markingKey: (c) Light-harvesting complexes (LHC): groups of pigment molecules bound to proteins in PS I and PS II that make up antennae.
options: photolysis of water
chemiosmotic hypothesis
light-harvesting complexes (LHC)
photophosphorylation

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of electron flow in the Z scheme: NADP⁺, PS I (P700), water, PS II (P680). Give a reason.
items.answer: water → PS II (P680) → PS I (P700) → NADP⁺
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order water → PS II (P680) → PS I (P700) → NADP⁺; 1 mark for the reason: Electrons from water pass to PS II, then via ETS to PS I and finally reduce NADP⁺.

items.stem: Explain the Z scheme of the light reaction. How is ATP produced by chemiosmosis?
items.answer: PS II (P680) absorbs light, electrons excited and passed through the ETS (cytochromes) downhill to PS I (P700); PS I electrons excited to another acceptor and pass to NADP⁺ forming NADPH; water split at PS II replaces electrons and releases O₂. Proton gradient: photolysis inside lumen, carrier pumps H⁺ into lumen, NADP reductase removes H⁺ from stroma; H⁺ flows out through CF₀ of ATP synthase; CF₁ makes ATP.
items.markingKey: 3 marks Z scheme; 2 marks chemiosmosis.

items.stem:
In an experiment, isolated chloroplasts were placed in light. When a chemical that made the thylakoid membrane leaky to protons was added, ATP formation stopped although electrons still flowed.
(i) Name the hypothesis that explains this result. (1 mark)
(ii) Where do protons accumulate during the light reaction? (1 mark)
(iii) Explain how the proton gradient leads to ATP synthesis. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Chemiosmotic hypothesis. (ii) In the lumen of the thylakoid. (iii) Protons diffuse back to the stroma through the CF₀ channel of ATP synthase; this causes a conformational change in CF₁, which synthesises ATP from ADP and Pi.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the light reaction is correct?
items.answer: The water-splitting complex is on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.
items.markingKey: (a) The water-splitting complex is on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane. The other statements are false. Only ATP is synthesised; NADPH is formed in non-cyclic photophosphorylation. Photolysis of water is associated with PS II. They are named in the order of their discovery, not their function.
options: The water-splitting complex is on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.
PS I and PS II are named in the order they act in electron flow.
Cyclic photophosphorylation produces both ATP and NADPH.
Photolysis of water is associated with PS I.

items.stem: What is meant by “PEP carboxylase (PEPcase)”?
items.answer: The primary CO₂-fixing enzyme in the mesophyll cells of C4 plants.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the primary CO₂-fixing enzyme in the mesophyll cells of C4 plants.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as C4 plant or C3 plant: maize, sorghum, sugarcane, wheat.
items.answer: maize – C4 plant; sorghum – C4 plant; sugarcane – C4 plant; wheat – C3 plant.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: maize – C4 plant; sorghum – C4 plant; sugarcane – C4 plant; wheat – C3 plant.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a C3 plant?
items.answer: maize
items.markingKey: (c) Maize is a C4 plant, not a C3 plant.
options: wheat
potato
maize
mustard

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Bundle sheath cells of C4 plants lack RuBisCO.”
items.answer: Bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCO; mesophyll cells lack it and have PEPcase.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCO; mesophyll cells lack it and have PEPcase.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of events in the C4 pathway?
items.answer: PEP accepts CO₂ in mesophyll → OAA formed → transported to bundle sheath → CO₂ released and enters Calvin cycle
items.markingKey: (b) PEP accepts CO₂ in mesophyll → OAA formed → transported to bundle sheath → CO₂ released and enters Calvin cycle. Hatch and Slack pathway.
options: OAA formed → CO₂ released and enters Calvin cycle → transported to bundle sheath → PEP accepts CO₂ in mesophyll
PEP accepts CO₂ in mesophyll → OAA formed → transported to bundle sheath → CO₂ released and enters Calvin cycle
OAA formed → PEP accepts CO₂ in mesophyll → transported to bundle sheath → CO₂ released and enters Calvin cycle
transported to bundle sheath → CO₂ released and enters Calvin cycle → OAA formed → PEP accepts CO₂ in mesophyll

items.stem: Calculate the number of turns of the Calvin cycle and the number of ATP and NADPH molecules needed to make 3 molecules of glucose in a C3 plant.
items.answer: 18 turns; 54 ATP and 36 NADPH
items.markingKey: One turn fixes one CO₂ and uses 3 ATP + 2 NADPH (1); one glucose needs 6 turns, so 3 glucose need 18 turns, 54 ATP and 36 NADPH (1).

items.stem:
Leaf sections of maize and wheat from a farm near Ludhiana were compared. Maize showed large cells with many chloroplasts around the veins; wheat did not.
(i) What is this special anatomy of maize called? (1 mark)
(ii) Which enzyme fixes CO₂ first in the mesophyll of maize? (1 mark)
(iii) Why is maize more productive than wheat at high temperatures and high light? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Kranz anatomy. (ii) PEP carboxylase (PEPcase). (iii) Maize is a C4 plant: CO₂ is concentrated in bundle sheath cells, so RuBisCO works as a carboxylase and photorespiration is avoided; the optimum temperature is higher.

items.stem: How many molecules of NADPH are needed to synthesise 3 molecules of glucose (18 CO₂ fixed) in a C3 plant?
items.markingKey: (c) Per CO₂: 3 ATP and 2 NADPH in the Calvin cycle (C4 plants use 2 extra ATP per CO₂). For 18 CO₂: NADPH = 36.

items.stem: Which of the following is a C3 plant?
items.answer: potato
items.markingKey: (a) Potato is a C3 plant; the others are not.
options: potato
Amaranthus
sugarcane
sorghum

items.stem: Describe the three stages of the Calvin cycle. Calculate the ATP and NADPH needed to make one glucose molecule.
items.answer: Carboxylation – CO₂ + RuBP → 2 PGA by RuBisCO; reduction – PGA reduced to carbohydrate using 2 ATP and 2 NADPH per CO₂; regeneration – RuBP regenerated using 1 ATP per CO₂. Per CO₂: 3 ATP, 2 NADPH; one glucose needs 6 turns: 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.
items.markingKey: 3 marks stages; 2 marks calculation.

items.stem: Calculate the number of turns of the Calvin cycle and the number of ATP and NADPH molecules needed to make 10 molecules of glucose in a C3 plant.
items.answer: 60 turns; 180 ATP and 120 NADPH
items.markingKey: One turn fixes one CO₂ and uses 3 ATP + 2 NADPH (1); one glucose needs 6 turns, so 10 glucose need 60 turns, 180 ATP and 120 NADPH (1).

items.stem: A plant shows these features: first stable product is OAA; photorespiration absent. Identify the type of plant. Give a reason.
items.answer: A C4 plant
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a C4 plant; 1 mark: the features first stable product is OAA; photorespiration absent are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the Calvin cycle and the C4 pathway is correct?
items.answer: Melvin Calvin used radioactive ¹⁴C in algal photosynthesis studies to discover the first CO₂ fixation product, PGA.
items.markingKey: (c) Melvin Calvin used radioactive ¹⁴C in algal photosynthesis studies to discover the first CO₂ fixation product, PGA. The other statements are false. The Calvin cycle occurs in all photosynthetic plants; C4 plants run it in bundle sheath cells. Bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCO; mesophyll cells lack it and have PEPcase. RuBP, a 5-carbon ketose sugar, is the primary acceptor.
options: The primary acceptor in C3 plants is a 3-carbon compound.
The Calvin cycle occurs only in C3 plants.
Melvin Calvin used radioactive ¹⁴C in algal photosynthesis studies to discover the first CO₂ fixation product, PGA.
Bundle sheath cells of C4 plants lack RuBisCO.

items.stem: Which of the following is a C3 plant?
items.answer: rice
items.markingKey: (a) Rice is a C3 plant; the others are not.
options: rice
Amaranthus
sugarcane
sorghum

items.stem: Calculate the number of turns of the Calvin cycle and the number of ATP and NADPH molecules needed to make 5 molecules of glucose in a C3 plant.
items.answer: 30 turns; 90 ATP and 60 NADPH
items.markingKey: One turn fixes one CO₂ and uses 3 ATP + 2 NADPH (1); one glucose needs 6 turns, so 5 glucose need 30 turns, 90 ATP and 60 NADPH (1).

items.stem: Define the term “limiting factor”.
items.answer: The factor that directly affects a process if its quantity is changed, being present at sub-optimal level.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the factor that directly affects a process if its quantity is changed, being present at sub-optimal level.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as external factor affecting photosynthesis or internal (plant) factor affecting photosynthesis: CO₂ concentration, mesophyll cells and chloroplasts, number, size, age and orientation of leaves, temperature.
items.answer: CO₂ concentration – external factor affecting photosynthesis; mesophyll cells and chloroplasts – internal (plant) factor affecting photosynthesis; number, size, age and orientation of leaves – internal (plant) factor affecting photosynthesis; temperature – external factor affecting photosynthesis.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: CO₂ concentration – external factor affecting photosynthesis; mesophyll cells and chloroplasts – internal (plant) factor affecting photosynthesis; number, size, age and orientation of leaves – internal (plant) factor affecting photosynthesis; temperature – external factor affecting photosynthesis.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Water stress has no effect on photosynthesis.
Reason (R): Photorespiration produces neither sugar nor ATP; it results in the release of CO₂ with the use of ATP.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Water stress causes stomata to close, reducing CO₂ availability, and leaves wilt. R is a true statement.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.answer: (i) Temperature (ii) tropical plants have a higher optimum than temperate plants (iii) very high intensity may break down chlorophyll; saturation at about 10% of full sunlight

items.stem: Which of the following statements about photorespiration and factors affecting photosynthesis is correct?

items.stem:

(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)

items.answer: (i) Photolysis of water (ii) supplies electrons to replace those lost by PS II (iii) O₂ is released; electrons from water reach NADP⁺

items.stem: Which of the following statements about photorespiration and factors affecting photosynthesis is correct?

Light is the most common limiting factor for photosynthesis in nature.

items.stem: Compare a C3 plant and a C4 plant on any three points.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about early experiments, the site of photosynthesis and pigments is correct?
items.answer: Julius von Sachs provided evidence that glucose is made in the green parts of plants and stored as starch.

Julius von Sachs provided evidence that glucose is made in the green parts of plants and stored as starch.
Photosynthesis occurs only in the leaves of plants.
The dark reactions of photosynthesis occur in the grana.
